It serves as the base for India’s natural gas reserves.
It is a vital maritime choke point for much of our LPG imports.
It is the site of a new, state-of-the-art LNG plant.
questions.explain: Ninety percent of our LPG imports flow through this volatile region, creating a 'just-in-time' supply chain vulnerability. If tensions flare up there, India's energy prices can swing wildly, which is a major headache for policymakers. That's why building a domestic pipeline network is so urgent.

questions.q: What is the primary constraint currently hindering the rapid expansion of PNG infrastructure in India?
options: Natural gas is too environmentally hazardous compared to LPG.
High investment needs for pipelines and challenges in land acquisition.
Lack of public demand for gaseous fuel.
The prohibitively high costs of gas exploration.
questions.explain: Building thousands of kilometers of pipelines isn't just expensive; it’s an absolute nightmare in terms of land acquisition laws. Despite these logistical hurdles, the push is ongoing to make it more convenient for the end-user. It's the ultimate 'energy transition' project for our urban centers.

questions.q: What does the term 'Just-in-Time' refer to regarding India’s current LNG system?
options: Limited domestic storage capacity, making the supply dependent on regular imports.
The ability to switch to coal within minutes during a shortage.
Rapid delivery of cooking gas via air transport.
The practice of ordering gas exactly one day before depletion.
questions.explain: Because we lack massive strategic stockpiles for LNG, we have to keep imports flowing consistently, leaving little margin for error. If a ship is delayed due to global weather or conflict, it affects domestic availability almost immediately. Strengthening our storage facilities is definitely a part of the government's long-term plan.
